title: オペレーティングシステム
subtitle: Operating Systems
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn the basic features of PC and workstation OS.
(2) Learn key OS concepts and functional components.
(3) Learn system programming techniques.
advice:
This is a basic operating systems course. We will cover the following materials:

1. Installing virtual machines and Linux
2. Linux advanced　command exercises
3. Programming with the basic UNIX system calls
4. Process management and scheduling
5. Memory management
6. File systems
7. UNIX system programming

Students are expected to bring their textbook, notebook PC, and other necessary materials to every class.
Students are expected to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class and on a regular basis.
requiredKnowledge:
This course requires the following knowledge/skills:
1. The units of “Programming 1” and “Programming 2” have been acquired.
2. Knowledge of basic logical operation.
3. Basic C programming skills.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basics of operating systems
Be able to explain the key points of the process and thread.
Be able to explain the key points of the memory management system.
Be able to explain the key points of the file system.
Be able to perform basic programming using Linux system calls.

lessons.content:
Chapter 1 Overview of OS and C programming:
Install Linux on your own notebook PC, and learn
 the overview of the OS concepts and functional
components.

Chapter 2 Process management 1:
(1)Process, job, and thread
(2)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 2 Process management 2:
(1)Process state transition
(2)fork system call
(3)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 2 Process management 3:
(1)Interprocess communication
(2)pipe system call
(3)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 2 Process management 4:
(1)Multithread programming
(2)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 3 Process scheduling:
(1)Scheduling algorithm
(2)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 4 Interrupt control:
(1)CPU running mode
(2)Context switching
(3)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 5 Virtual Memory 1:
(1)Basic memory management
(2)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 5 Virtual Memory 2:
(1)Features of virtual memory system
(2)Address translation technologies
(3)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 5 Virtual Memory 3:
(1)Page replacement algorithm
(2)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 6 I/O and file systems 1:
(1)Directory layout and path
(2)Linux file system(i-node)
(3)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 6 I/O and file systems 2:
(1)Sequential and random access
(2)File permissions
(3)Linux advanced command exercises

Chapter 6 I/O and file systems 3:
(1)System calls used for I/O
(2)File descriptor
(3)Linux advanced command exercises
